alternatives.name: COLLECTION_ROOT_REPOSITORY_WITH_PROTOTYPE_EXCLUSIONS
tradeoffs: Would place the canonical platform and current cross-project material under one root.
Creates a high accidental-staging and deletion risk because the collection contains prototypes, a dirty nested Git repository, caches, logs, environments, and LFS pointers.
Requires broad exclusion rules whose failure could capture user-owned or sensitive state.
Makes clean-clone and release provenance depend on a collection folder that is not itself a coherent product.

alternatives.name: DEDICATED_CHILD_REPOSITORY_SIBLING_TO_PROTOTYPES
tradeoffs: Creates one narrow repository as a direct child of the collection root and a sibling of every prototype.
Versions canonical governance and the new foundation subject together without placing prototypes under its Git boundary.
Keeps prototype references logical and external until a later migration decision is separately authorized.
Requires an explicit document-copy registration step and a protected root-ID path map, which is acceptable and auditable.

alternatives.name: GOVERNED_SUPERPROJECT_WITH_REFERENCED_PROTOTYPES
tradeoffs: Could later preserve independent prototype history through submodules or another deliberate reference mechanism.
Cannot safely begin while one prototype is dirty and the other prototypes lack reconciled repository identity and ownership.
Introduces remote, nested-repository, and clean-clone complexity that Phase 0 does not need.
May be reconsidered only after separate ownership, licensing, remote, and preservation decisions.

alternatives.name: EXISTING_PROTOTYPE_AS_INTEGRATED_PLATFORM_ROOT
tradeoffs: Would reuse an existing repository history.
Would make one prototype's architecture, licensing, remote, nested paths, and dirty working tree own the broader platform without evidence that it should.
Would create unacceptable risk of staging or changing current user-owned Short Squeeze modifications and untracked files.
Conflicts with the canonical direction to preserve prototypes as external references until separately migrated.

negative: Governed documents must be registered by exact-byte copy into the new boundary after authorization.
Prototype references remain external and cannot be assumed available in a clean clone.
A separately protected path map is required for execution because published evidence contains no absolute host path.
positive: The new Git boundary contains only canonical governance, Phase 0 structural source, tests, tools, and evidence selected by approved manifests.
No existing prototype, nested Git repository, background log, cache, environment, or data object becomes part of the new repository.
Rollback can remove one newly created boundary without touching prototypes when all rollback preconditions hold.
Clean-clone, offline-install, and release provenance can be evaluated against one coherent subject.

decision.governed_document_placement: Canonical specifications, controlling plans, decisions, governance records, and later Phase 0 evidence reside under repository-relative docs/superpowers paths. Exact approved bytes are copied; approved source artifacts are never edited in place.
decision.large_data_and_lfs_policy: No raw market data, file at least 10 MiB, Git LFS pointer, Git LFS object, or data directory from a prototype is included. Any future fixture requires a separate data-feasibility authorization outside Phase 0.
decision.logs_caches_generated_policy: Logs, caches, virtual environments, node_modules, build output, temporary directories, generated test repositories, coverage output, and editor state are excluded from the repository and Phase 0 evidence unless a later approved evidence manifest names a sanitized generated artifact explicitly.
decision.nested_repository_policy: Every existing repository remains external. The Short Squeeze repository and generated test-fixture .git markers are neither nested, linked, vendored, staged, nor referenced through Git mechanisms by Phase 0.
decision.prototype_policy: All five prototypes are excluded physical siblings. They may be named only as sanitized preservation subjects and non-executable references. No source, configuration, history, data, environment, or generated artifact is copied or imported.
decision.remote_policy: NONE. No remote is created, configured, queried, fetched, pulled, pushed, cloned, or otherwise contacted during boundary establishment or Phase 0 Steps 9 through 13.
decision.repository_root_model: A new dedicated Git repository resolved from opaque ROOT-2E7C91F4, physically a direct child of collection root ROOT-8A4D17C2 and a sibling of every prototype.

effectivity.approval_requirement: Attributable exact-hash approval by PROJECT-PRINCIPAL-001 acting as PROJECT_OWNER and RELEASE_OWNER.
effectivity.non_authorization_statement: Acceptance selects the root model only. It does not create a directory, initialize Git, configure a remote, copy a document, move a path, edit a repository, stage, commit, branch, or create a worktree.

preservation_evidence.after_operation_requirement: Recompute the frozen safe inventory, sensitive metadata, Git identity/status, LFS-pointer metadata, and root-entry classification after boundary establishment and publish a sanitized difference report.
preservation_evidence.pass_rule: No prototype or preexisting collection-root entry changes; the only allowed root delta is creation of ROOT-2E7C91F4. Excluded volatile drift is reported separately and cannot conceal another difference.

rollback.allowed_target: Only ROOT-2E7C91F4 when it was absent before the authorized operation and contains no user-created content outside the operation manifest.
rollback.method: Verify the resolved target remains the authorized direct child, archive the failure report outside the target, then remove only that new boundary. Never roll back by touching a prototype.
